name: Clean vs Polluted Places: Evoked Pleasure and Approach Desire
description: Faithful replication with the original photographs: participants see 116 photographs of everyday urban and rural places, 58 clean and 58 with visible waste (polluted), some with people and some without, in random order. Each photo is shown for 3 s and is followed by two questions in fixed order: evoked pleasure (1 = very unpleasant, 5 = neutral, 9 = very pleasant) and approach desire, how much the scene makes them want to be in it (1 = withdrawal desire, 5 = neutral, 9 = approach desire). Age and gender are asked at the end. Rebuilt from Beaumont, Lelard, Mouras & Granon (2020), Evoked pleasure and approach-avoidance in response to pollution, PLOS ONE 15(6): e0234210, with the photo database from its S2 File (CC BY 4.0; taken by a professional photographer for the study). Image ids: urb/rur = urban/rural, pers = with people, propre = clean, sale = polluted, then the authors' number. Analysis as in the paper: mean pleasure and approach desire per condition (clean vs polluted, repeated-measures ANOVA), per-picture one-sample t-tests against 6 (clean) or 4 (polluted) to select unambiguous pictures, and condition x context (urban/rural), x people, x gender and x age group (under 35, 35-54, 55 and over) effects on pleasure. Differences from the original study: (1) online rather than in the lab with E-Prime and keyboard responses; (2) photos are resized to 1024 px; (3) the question wording is ours, built from the paper's scale names and anchors (its Fig 2); (4) age is asked as a number (the paper analysed three age groups) and the gender options are ours.
author: Beaumont, Lelard, Mouras & Granon
